children: Shares in Nvidia rose over 3% early Wednesday.
Shares in Nvidia climbed on Wednesday as investors digested the chip giant's better-than-expected third-quarter financial results. But some analysts say there's more volatility for the stock to come.

The company's stock (NVDA) advanced over 3% in early trading on Wednesday, a bit off the peak following Nvidia reporting data-center revenue more than doubling on Tuesday night. It also lifted its revenue for the next quarter to $130 billion, beating Wall Street consensus.

JPMorgan analysts, led by Harlan Sur, warned in a Wednesday note that the stock will likely remain volatile in the near-term. Despite the company beating forecasts on several fronts and raising its targets, management left several key risks unaddressed during the earnings call - namely the exclusion of China from its outlook, ongoing financing and artificial-intelligence buildout concerns and supply-chain scaling challenges as Nvidia searches for a new CEO following Jensen Huang's resignation.

A team at Goldman Sachs, headed by James Schneider, said they see the stock maintaining its gains following the strong set of results. "Although significant uncertainty remains on several fronts, we believe management's commentary should bolster investor confidence in the fundamental outlook for both Nvidia's business and the broader AI ecosystem across a number of dimensions," they wrote in a Tuesday note. They noted Nvidia's reiterated dedication to returns on investments for shareholders, with authorization to buy back $227 billion before the end of calendar year 2027.

"The strength we continue to see in the business is not a surprise, but the willingness to provide the level of forward-looking commentary we heard on the call was a significant positive," added a Morgan Stanley group, including Joseph Moore, U.S. semiconductor industry analyst.
